Analysis & Results

To operationalise the central research question this study employs a set of exploratory data visualisations.These ﬁgures correspond to Key analytical variables, including ICT economic performance, innovation and ownership, and geographical distribution of investment. Taken together, these ﬁgures provide empirical insight into whether South Africa participates in the global technological economy as a producer or remains structurally positioned as a consumer.

Figure 1: Temporal Trends in ICT Exports and Imports in South Africa

To assess South Africa’s position in global ICT trade, the following figure compares ICT exports and imports over time.

ict_trade_exports_imports_billion_zar_data <- tech_dev_SA %>% 
  filter(str_detect(indicator, regex("ICT_Trade", ignore_case = TRUE)))
ict_trade_exports_imports_billion_zar_data
head(ict_trade_exports_imports_billion_zar_data)
line_graph_colours <- c("ICT_Trade_Exports_Billion_ZAR" = "#1b9e77",
                        "ICT_Trade_Imports_Billion_ZAR" = "#d95f02")
line_graph_colours
## ICT_Trade_Exports_Billion_ZAR ICT_Trade_Imports_Billion_ZAR 
##                     "#1b9e77"                     "#d95f02"
line_graph_indicator_labels <- c(
  "ICT_Trade_Exports_Billion_ZAR" = "ICT Exports (Billion ZAR)",
  "ICT_Trade_Imports_Billion_ZAR" = "ICT Imports (Billion ZAR)"
)
line_graph_indicator_labels
## ICT_Trade_Exports_Billion_ZAR ICT_Trade_Imports_Billion_ZAR 
##   "ICT Exports (Billion ZAR)"   "ICT Imports (Billion ZAR)"
ict_trade_line_graph <- ict_trade_exports_imports_billion_zar_data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value, colour = indicator, group = indicator)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = line_graph_colours,
    labels = line_graph_indicator_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "More Bought Than Built",
    subtitle = "ICT Exports vs Imports Over Time",
    x = "Year", y = "Billion ZAR", colour = "Indicator Type"
  ) +
 theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16, colour = "#22223B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, color = "grey30", face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.21, 0.80),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
ict_trade_line_graph

ggsave("fig1_ICT_Exports_vs_Imports_Over_Time.png", ict_trade_line_graph, width = 9.5, height = 7, dpi = 300)

Note. Adapted from International trade in digitally deliverable services, value, shares and growth, annual (analytical) - Telecommunications, computer, and information services (Exports; Imports), by UNCTADStat (United Nations Conference on Trade and Development), 2025a, 2025b, UNCTADStat Data centre.

Figure 1

To assess South Africa’s position within global ICT trade and its role as a producer or consumer of technological Goods, Figure “ICT Exports vs Imports Over Time” illustrates the persistent trade imbalance in the South African ICT sector.The data reveals a growing trade deﬁcit in the ICT sector, with imports consistently exceeding exports across the entire period from 2010 to 2024. While both types of values show an overall increase, the growth rate of ICT imports has been signiﬁcantly steeper than that of exports. This has resulted in a widening trade gap from approximately 4.5 Billion ZAR in 2010 to over 46 Billion ZAR in 2024. This suggests that South Africa’s participation in the ICT sector is structurally skewed toward consumption rather than production.

Figure 2: ICT Exports and Imports as a Percentage of Total Goods Trade in South Africa

To contextualise this trade imbalance within the broader economy, the following figure shows ICT imports and exports as a percentage of total goods trade.

ict_exports_imports_total_goods_percent_data <- tech_dev_SA %>% 
  filter(str_detect(indicator, regex("ICT_exports|ICT_imports", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% 
  mutate(indicator = str_trim(indicator))

ict_exports_imports_total_goods_percent_data
head(ict_exports_imports_total_goods_percent_data)
indicator_labels_new <- c("ICT_exports_total_goods_percent" = "ICT Exports",
"ICT_imports_total_goods_percent" = "ICT Imports")

indicator_labels_new
## ICT_exports_total_goods_percent ICT_imports_total_goods_percent 
##                   "ICT Exports"                   "ICT Imports"
ict_wide <- ict_exports_imports_total_goods_percent_data %>%
  select(year, indicator, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = value)
ict_gap_plot <- ggplot(ict_wide, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ICT_exports_total_goods_percent,
                   ymax = ICT_imports_total_goods_percent,
                   fill = "Gap"), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ICT_exports_total_goods_percent, colour = "ICT Exports"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ICT_imports_total_goods_percent, colour = "ICT Imports"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ICT_exports_total_goods_percent, colour = "ICT Exports"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ICT_imports_total_goods_percent, colour = "ICT Imports"), size = 2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(begin = 0, end = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Gap" = "grey50"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Baked Into the Economy",
    subtitle = "ICT Imports and Exports as % of Total Goods",
    x = "Year", y = "Percentage of Total Goods", colour = "Indicator Type"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
 theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16, colour = "#22223B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, color = "grey30", face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.84, 0.80),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ict_gap_plot

ggsave("fig2_ICT_Imports_and_Exports_as_pct_of_Total_Goods.png", ict_gap_plot, width = 9.5, height = 7, dpi = 300)

Note. Adapted from ICT goods exports (percent of total goods exports) - South Africa and ICT goods imports (percent total goods imports) - South Africa, by World Bank Group, n.d.-a, n.d.-b, World Development Indicators.

Figure 2

To contextualise this imbalance within the broader economy, Figure “ICT Imports and Exports as % of Total Goods” further articulates the imbalance shown in Figure 1; ICT imports consistently account for a signiﬁcantly larger percentage of total goods imported, compared to exported throughout the entire period. Throughout most of the years, the percentage of total goods accounted for by ICT imports roughly doubles that of ICT exports. This reveals a signiﬁcant and substantial reliance on foreign technology goods within the broader South African economy. This reinforces the argument that reliance on foreign ICT goods is not isolated but structurally embedded within South Africa’s national economy.

Figure 3

To evaluate whether South Africa is investing in building its own technological capacity, Figure “Investment in ICT (as % of Total Primary Sector Investment)” is measured as a percentage of the total of investment ﬂow into the primary sectors at the forefront of the South African economy and growth. There are inconsistencies which suggest instability in allocation of resources towards and within said sector. Despite these ﬂuctuations, ICT investment share in the investment market, speciﬁcally, and the South African economy, in general, continues to have an upward trajectory. This suggests that although ICT is recognised as important in South Africa, investment patterns may not yet support the stable, long-term development of a locally driven technological sector.

Figure 4: Spatial Distribution of Investee Company Locations in South Africa

To examine internal inequalities in technological development, the following ﬁgure shows the geographic distribution of ICT investment across South Africa.

sa <- gadm(country = "ZAF", level = 1, path = tempdir()) |> st_as_sf()

bubbles <- tibble::tibble(
  label = c("Western Cape", "Gauteng", "KwaZulu-Natal",
            "Rest of SA\n(6 provinces, aggregate)"),
  lon   = c(21.0, 28.05, 30.5, 26.7),
  lat   = c(-33.2, -26.05, -28.5, -28.9),
  share = c(53.0, 33.8, 3.2, 3.5)
)

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = sa, fill = "white", color = "#3D5A80", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = bubbles,
             aes(x = lon, y = lat, size = share, fill = share),
             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 1.2, alpha = 1) +
  geom_label_repel(data = bubbles,
                    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = paste0(label, ": ", share, "%")),
                    size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", color = "black",
                    fill = "white", label.size = 0.3, label.r = unit(0.15, "lines"),
                    segment.color = "#3D5A80", segment.size = 0.4) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 30), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Where the Capital Lands",
    subtitle = "ICT investee company locations by province, *2013 - 2024*",
    caption = "***Note***. Circle size = Share (%). *'Rest of SA'* combines six provinces (Eastern Cape, Free State, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West, Northern Cape) - the source data reports no per-province breakdown for them. An additional 6.5% of investees are based outside South Africa and are not mapped here. Adapted from SAVCA 2025 Venture Capital Industry Survey, p.12."

  ) +
  coord_sf(clip = "off") +
  theme_void(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#22223B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, color = "grey30", face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_textbox_simple(
      size = 7.5, color = "grey40", hjust = 0, halign = 0,
      width = unit(1, "npc"), lineheight = 1.2,
      padding = margin(18, 0, 0, 0)   # was margin(4, 0, 0, 0) — more top space
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 15, 10)  # slightly more bottom room too
  )

p

ggsave("fig4_ICT_investee_company_locations_by_province_2013_2024.png", p, width = 9.5, height = 7, dpi = 300)

Note. Adapted from SAVCA 2025 Venture Capital Industry Survey, by Southern African Venture Capital and Private Equity Association (SAVCA), 2025, p.12.

Figure 4

To examine internal inequalities in technological development, Figure“ Distribution of Investee Company Locations (2013-2024)” reveals the Western Cape and Gauteng receiving the vast majority of the total of Investments (foreign and national) during this period. Remain in provinces like KwaZulu Natal and the Rest of South Africa receive only a minute fraction of the total of investments ﬂowing into the country. This highlights a signiﬁcant geographic disparity in the distribution of capital.This highlights a signiﬁcant spatial concentration of capital, raising questions about unequal access to technological development and reinforcing the study’s concern with ‘who gets to evolve and who doesn’t’.

Figure 5: Comparative Trends in Domestic and Foreign Patent Activity

To assess the extent of locally driven innovation and ownership, the following figure compares domestic and foreign patent filings in South Africa.

patent_data <- tech_dev_SA %>% 
  filter(str_detect(indicator, regex("patent", ignore_case = TRUE)))
patent_data
head(patent_data)
patent_activity <- patent_data %>% 
  filter(str_detect(indicator, regex("patent", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year),
         value = as.numeric(value))

year_breaks <- seq(min(patent_activity$year, na.rm = TRUE),
                    max(patent_activity$year, na.rm = TRUE), by = 5)
patent_activity <- ggplot(patent_activity, aes(x = factor(year), y = indicator, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Number of\nPatents") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = as.character(year_breaks), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = c("patent_applications_nonresidents" = "Foreign Patents",
                               "patent_applications_residents" = "Domestic Patents"),
                    expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "Where the Ideas Come From",
    subtitle = "**Patent Activity: Domestic vs. Foreign (1980 - 2021)**<br><span style='font-size:9pt;color:gray40'>Number of Patents Filed by Origin</span>",
    x = "Year", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#22223B"),
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(size = 11, lineheight = 1.4, margin = margin(b = 10), hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30"),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(4, "pt"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
    legend.position = "right",
legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )

patent_activity 

ggsave("fig5_Patent_Activity_Domestic_vs_Foreign_1980_2021.png", patent_activity, width = 9.5, height = 7, dpi = 300)

Note. Adapted from Patent applications, nonresidents - South Africa and Patent applications, residents - South Africa, by World Bank Group, n.d.-c, n.d.-d, World Development Indicators.

Figure 5

To assess the extent to which innovation and ownership is locally generated, Figure “Patent Activity: Domestic vs. Foreign (1980-2021)” reveals that the South African ICT and Technology patent landscape is dominated by non-resident ﬁlings; therefore, dramatically exceeding ﬁlings made by domestic residents. While non-resident applications are robust, domestic patent applications remain low. This signals a somewhat nascent internal intellectual property generation pipeline and culture, relative to external patent registrations and ICT environments in other nations; suggesting limited domestic innovation capacity and supports the argument That technological ownership remains concentrated outside South Africa.

Taken together, the visualisations provide a multi-dimensional empirical account of South Africa’s ICT sector, demonstrating that structural dependence operates across trade, investment, geography, and innovation.

Rather than functioning as an autonomous site of technological production, the sector reﬂects broader historical and global inequalities that continue to shape the country’s developmental trajectory.
